text.en:
Hari covered one leaf of a potted plant with black paper for three days. After a test with iodine the covered part stayed yellow-brown while the uncovered part turned blue-black.
"The leaf made starch only where light fell," said his teacher.

Plants make their own food by photosynthesis. Leaves take in carbon dioxide from the air through tiny holes called stomata, roots take in water from the soil, and chlorophyll, the green substance in leaves, captures sunlight energy.
Carbon dioxide + water, in sunlight and chlorophyll, gives glucose (food) and oxygen. Glucose is stored as starch. The oxygen is released into the air.
Water and minerals go up from roots through tubes called xylem. Food made in leaves is carried to all parts through tubes called phloem. Plants also lose water as vapour through stomata, which is called transpiration.
Plants make food by photosynthesis in their leaves.
Carbon dioxide, water and sunlight go in. Glucose and oxygen come out.
Water travels up through the xylem. Food travels through the phloem.
Plants lose water vapour through stomata. This is transpiration.

problem.en: Why does a plant kept in the dark for many days become weak?

text.en: Without light the leaves cannot make food.
So the plant becomes weak and may die.

prompt.en: A friend says plants take their food from the soil. How will you correct this?

requiredIdeas.en: Plants make their own food in the leaves by photosynthesis.
The soil gives water and minerals, not food.

points.en: Photosynthesis: carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen in sunlight.
Xylem carries water up; phloem carries food.
Transpiration is water loss through stomata.
